extracted.intended_audience: patent applicants and registered patent practitioners (attorneys/agents)
extracted.subtask_description: Procedures and requirements for use of USPTO Search Room and Technology Center facilities, and the rules for obtaining filing-date benefits via Express Mail, Certificates of Mailing/Transmission (37 CFR 1.8 and 1.10), and petitions relating to postal interruptions or emergencies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Search Room security and conduct rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Whenever a marked document is transported past the sensing equipment, USPTO officials and security guards will be alerted. Persons triggering the alarm will be asked to cooperate in identifying the source for the alarm.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Failure to cooperate when the alarm is triggered could result in detention, seizure of briefcases, or other legal measures. The Search Room regulations are reprinted in a regulation brochure available in the Search Room and will be strictly enforced.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of TC Facilities: subject to federal property conduct regulations
rubrics_metrics.description: All persons using TC facilities are subject to the Regulations Governing Conduct on Federal Property, as specified in 41 CFR Subpart 101-20.3.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Posted Official Notices must be complied with. The TC facilities are defined locations and use is limited to regular USPTO business hours.

rubrics_metrics.name: User Pass display and nontransferability
rubrics_metrics.description: A valid User Pass must be prominently displayed when in the TC Facilities. User Passes are nontransferable and must be surrendered upon request to authorized officials.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Supervisory Patent Examiners and TC Directors may demand surrender of User Passes on-the-spot and must be notified and followed up with a memorandum when exercised.

rubrics_metrics.name: Registration with TC Receptionist
rubrics_metrics.description: All persons holding User Passes must register with the TC Receptionist, unless otherwise directed, in each TC.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If an individual is not wearing a User's Pass, identification should be requested; refusal should be reported to a supervisor.

rubrics_metrics.name: No removal of USPTO records without authorization
rubrics_metrics.description: No records or other documents of the USPTO shall be removed from the TC Facilities except by express written authorization by an authorized official in the TC where the material resides.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Violation may lead to denial of facility use, prosecution, and referral to Office of Enrollment and Discipline under 37 CFR Part 10.

rubrics_metrics.name: Smoking restricted to designated areas
rubrics_metrics.description: Smoking is not permitted except in designated areas.

rubrics_metrics.name: Food and beverages restricted to designated areas
rubrics_metrics.description: No food or beverages in any form are to be consumed except in designated areas.

rubrics_metrics.name: Noise and disruptive activity prohibited
rubrics_metrics.description: Loud talking, use of radios, and any other form of activity which may disturb other members of the public or Office personnel are forbidden.

rubrics_metrics.name: Children must not disturb others
rubrics_metrics.description: Children brought into the TC Facilities must not be allowed to disturb others.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of equipment requires prior permission
rubrics_metrics.description: The presence or use of equipment such as dictation equipment, reproducing machines, typewriters, and photographic equipment is prohibited without prior permission from an authorized official in the TC where the use is intended.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use is permitted only where it does not conflict with noise/disturbance regulations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Search of packages and personal effects
rubrics_metrics.description: All packages, briefcases, or other personal effects brought into the TC Facilities are subject to search by authorized officials upon request and must be removed when leaving the TC Facilities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compliance with verbal requests from authorized officials
rubrics_metrics.description: All verbal requests for compliance with these regulations or other posted USPTO Notices pertaining to activity in the TC Facilities, when made by authorized officials, must be promptly complied with.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a verbal request is not complied with, note the individual's name and User's Pass number if possible and report the incident to appropriate supervisory personnel.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consequences for violating TC/Search Room regulations
rubrics_metrics.description: Persons violating these regulations may be denied the use of the facilities in the TC and Patent Search Room, and may further be subject to prosecution under the Criminal Code.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Additionally, the name of any person violating these regulations who is registered to practice before the USPTO may be forwarded to the Office of Enrollment and Discipline for action under 37 CFR Part 10.

rubrics_metrics.name: 35 U.S.C. 21 filing-date rule for postal interruptions/emergencies
rubrics_metrics.description: The Director may by rule prescribe that any paper or fee required to be filed in the USPTO will be considered filed on the date it was deposited with the USPS or would have been deposited but for postal service interruptions or emergencies designated by the Director.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Announcements and instructions will be posted on the USPTO website and Official Gazette when such events occur; authority found in 35 U.S.C. 21(a).

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 CFR 1.10(g) petition when correspondence returned by USPS
rubrics_metrics.description: A person whose Express Mail correspondence was returned by the USPS due to an interruption or emergency may petition the Director to consider it filed provided certain conditions are met.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Conditions include: (1) petition filed promptly after becoming aware of the return; (2) Express Mail label number was placed on the papers prior to original mailing; (3) petition includes the original correspondence or copy showing the label number and a copy of the Express Mail label showing the date-in; (4) petition includes a statement establishing to the Director's satisfaction the original deposit and that the correspondence is the original or a true copy. The Office may require additional evidence.

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 CFR 1.10(h) petition when USPS refuses deposit
rubrics_metrics.description: A person whose Express Mail correspondence was refused by a USPS employee due to an interruption or emergency may petition the Director to consider it filed provided conditions are met.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Conditions include: (1) petition filed promptly after becoming aware of the refusal; (2) Express Mail label number was placed on the papers prior to the attempted mailing; (3) petition includes the original correspondence or a copy showing the label number; (4) petition includes a statement by the person who attempted deposit establishing the attempt and that the correspondence is the original or a true copy. The Office may require additional evidence.

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 CFR 1.10(i) petition when unable to deposit due to designated interruption
rubrics_metrics.description: A person unable to deposit correspondence with the USPS due to a designated interruption or emergency may petition the Director to consider it filed provided conditions are met.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Conditions include: (1) petition filed promptly in a manner designated by the Director; (2) petition includes the original correspondence or a copy; (3) petition includes a statement establishing that the correspondence would have been deposited but for the designated interruption and that it is the original or a true copy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope limitation of 35 U.S.C. 21 and 37 CFR 1.10
rubrics_metrics.description: The provisions of 35 U.S.C. 21(a) and 37 CFR 1.10(g)-(i) apply only to postal interruptions and emergencies designated by the Director, not to other exigencies (e.g., computer or word processing failures, inaccessibility of non-USPS offices).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The statute requires the correspondence was complete and ready to be deposited with the USPS on the requested filing date and that it could not have been deposited for the sole reason of the designated postal interruption or emergency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recommendation to file by facsimile, Certificate, or EFS
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants are cautioned and advised that they should consider filing correspondence by facsimile when permitted, using a Certificate of Mailing or Transmission under 37 CFR 1.8 when permitted, or submitting via the Electronic Filing System (EFS) where available.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Office strongly recommends filing new applications by Express Mail (37 CFR 1.10) because such correspondence will be accorded the USPS deposit date as the filing date. New applications cannot be transmitted by facsimile for filing date purposes.

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 CFR 1.8 main rule for Certificate of Mailing/Transmission
rubrics_metrics.description: Correspondence will be considered timely filed if: (i) it is mailed or transmitted prior to expiration by either (A) addressed as set out in § 1.1(a) and deposited with the USPS with sufficient postage as first class mail, or (B) transmitted by facsimile in accordance with § 1.6(d); and (ii) the correspondence includes a certificate stating the date of deposit or transmission and the signer should have reasonable basis to expect mailing/transmission on or before the date indicated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The actual date of receipt will be used for other purposes. The procedure does not apply to certain enumerated exceptions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exceptions to Certificate of Mailing/Transmission benefits (37 CFR 1.8(a)(2))
rubrics_metrics.description: The Certificate of Mailing/Transmission practice does not apply to: (A) filing a national patent application specification and drawing or other correspondence for obtaining an application filing date (including CPA under §1.53(d)); (C) papers filed in contested cases before the Board; (D) filing an international application for patent; (E) filing correspondence in an international application before U.S. RO/ISA/IPEA; (F) filing a copy of the international application and national fee to enter national stage; and correspondence in disciplinary proceedings under part 10.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See full list in 37 CFR 1.8(a)(2)(i)-(iii) for specifics and reserved items.

rubrics_metrics.name: Remedy when certificate filed but Office has no evidence of receipt (37 CFR 1.8(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: If correspondence certified as mailed/transmitted is not received after a reasonable time, the correspondence will be considered timely if the party: (1) informs the Office promptly of the previous mailing/transmission; (2) supplies an additional copy of the previously mailed/transmitted correspondence and certificate; and (3) includes a statement attesting on a personal knowledge basis or to the Director's satisfaction the prior timely mailing/transmission. For facsimile, the sending unit's report may be used to support the statement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Office may require additional evidence to determine timeliness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Suggested format and content of Certificate of Mailing and Certificate of Transmission
rubrics_metrics.description: Suggested formats are provided for both certificates including the certification wording, the address to which mail must be deposited, and fields for date, typed name, signature, and registration number.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The certification may be included with all correspondence and proper use will result in communication being considered timely if within the required period for reply. The Certificate of Mailing procedure does not apply to papers mailed in a foreign country; Certificate of Transmission may apply to foreign transmissions if not prohibited.

rubrics_metrics.name: Signature and placement requirements for certification (¶ 5.02)
rubrics_metrics.description: The certification requires a signature. If the certification appears on a paper that requires a signature, two signatures are required — one for the paper and one for the certification. Preferred that the certificate be signed by the applicant, assignee, or registered practitioner.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When possible the certification should appear on the paper being submitted. If on a separate sheet, that sheet must be signed and fully identify and be securely attached to the paper (include application number, filing date, and type of paper). An unsigned certification will not be acceptable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Separate certifications for multiple papers/applications
rubrics_metrics.description: When correspondence includes papers for more than one application or papers for various parts of the Office, each paper must have its own certification as a part thereof or attached thereto.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Although some forms may contain a Certificate of Mailing, a separate Certificate is required for all papers included with that form (e.g., replacement drawings). Checks do not require certification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of stamped certification recommended
rubrics_metrics.description: Some practitioners place the certification language on the first page with an inked stamp.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such practice is encouraged because the certification is readily visible and forms an integral part of the paper.

rubrics_metrics.name: Office Mail Center handling and limitations on benefits
rubrics_metrics.description: The Mail Center will date stamp the actual date of receipt of all papers received by mail. Benefits of 37 CFR 1.8 or 1.10 apply only to documents delivered by the U.S. Postal Service.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When documents containing a Certificate or Express Mail label were delivered by commercial couriers or hand-carried, Mail Center personnel will place a notice indicating that benefits do not apply.

rubrics_metrics.name: Processing area procedures and notations for certificates
rubrics_metrics.description: When papers are received in specific Office locations, the date of receipt is stamped per 37 CFR 1.6(a). If a paper is received after the period for reply, inspectors should check for a Certificate; if found and dated within the period, the paper is considered timely and notation “C of Mail” or “C of Fax” with the certificate date should be placed adjacent to the Office date stamp and in the file wrapper.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the certificate date is after the period for reply, the paper is untimely and no notation need be made. For Image File Wrapper processing, follow IFW Manual.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling of hand-delivered papers claiming certificate benefits
rubrics_metrics.description: Office personnel receiving a hand-delivered paper should inspect it to ensure that the benefits of 37 CFR 1.8 or Express Mail are not accorded in error.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If such a paper contains a certificate or Express Mail label but was delivered other than by USPS, the words “HAND DELIVERED” should be written adjacent to the date stamp and applicant notified when benefits are denied.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form paragraph and notification when Certificate benefits denied (¶ 5.04)
rubrics_metrics.description: When correspondence contains a Certificate of Mailing under 37 CFR 1.8 or requests Express Mail benefits under 37 CFR 1.10 but was not deposited with the U.S. Postal Service, a form paragraph (¶ 5.04) should be used to notify applicant that the paper is not entitled to the benefits and the Office receipt date is used to determine timeliness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Misuse of a Certificate or improperly claiming Express Mail benefits that appears to be more than a one-time inadvertent error should be brought to the attention of the Office of Enrollment and Discipline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Original mailed paper not delivered: handling under 37 CFR 1.8(b) and (c)
rubrics_metrics.description: Paragraphs (b) and (c) of 37 CFR 1.8 concern papers timely deposited but never received by the Office. For submissions under these paragraphs, the sufficiency should be determined by the TC Director; the statement required by 37 CFR 1.8(b)(3) is no longer required to be verified.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: TCs should consider such submissions and determine sufficiency according to the guidance provided.
